title: GAIA-v2-LILT: Multilingual Adaptation of Agent Benchmark beyond Translation

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing autonomous agent success rates on original English benchmarks against machine-translated and fully audited multilingual versions across five non-English languages to quantify English-centric performance gaps and benchmark-induced measurement errors.

Measuring the change in model accuracy (result flipping rates) after localizing source-region assumptions, such as geography, measurement units, policy logic, and social norms, to match the target language's cultural context.

Assessing the impact of human fluency bias and LLM self-preference by measuring how frequently correcting stylistic fluency versus functional or cultural alignment actually flips the model's task evaluation outcome.
